newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi Sec admits sokaiya payoff--govt source.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi Sec admits sokaiya payoff--govt source.

text.p: Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd has generally admitted to allegations of making payoffs to a corporate client widely known to be connected to corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike for losses the client suffered in securities trading, a government source close to the investigation told reporters on Wednesday.
The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) and prosecutors raided the brokerage earlier on Wednesday for alleged violations of Japanese securities laws.

According to the source, Yamaichi is suspected of making a 79 million yen payoff to cover for losses the corporate client incurred in securities trading which amounted to between 30 and 50 million yen.

The client, which had a discretionary account with Yamaichi, suffered losses mainly in stock trading in the Tokyo market. The payoff was made from profits that Yamaichi made in Nikkei futures traded on SIMEX. Payoffs were made several times, mainly in January 1995, the source said.
The client suffered losses during the six-month period beginning in June 1994, the source said.
Yamaichi itself and several of its employees were involved in the payoffs, he said.
The source declined to comment when asked whether similar investigations were being made of Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
The SESC's last regular inspection of Yamaichi was conducted in November 1995, but it did not uncover any such illicit deals during that inspection, he said.
